Hi Lydia — thanks for the heads up and the clear timeline. Great opportunity — congrats on the pilot win. I’ve sketched three pragmatic paths (high level) so procurement can pick the fastest route:

Option A — Ad-hoc add-on (fastest provisioning)
- Immediate capacity add-on at list unit price
- Pro-rata invoice for the remainder of current term
- No change to renewal pricing
- Use when you need capacity immediately and want minimal paperwork

Option B — Annualize and co-term (best unit economics)
- Convert add-on to a 12-month uplift that co-terms with your existing renewal date
- Blended discount on uplift tiered by size: 0–250k units: 10% / 250k–1M: 18% / >1M: 24%
- Pro-rata credit applied from effective date to next invoice period (so billing aligns)

Option C — Bridge voucher + commit (short-term relief)
- One-time usage voucher to cover initial Q4 overage (e.g., $10k credit)
- Followed by a conversion option to a committed uplift within 30 days for an additional discount (typically +5–6% on top of tier)

I’ve attached a short options spreadsheet and a draft amendment template to make legal’s job easier.

Next steps I suggest: 1) confirm which option you prefer, 2) tell us the expected uplift size (rough bands are fine), 3) we’ll produce a redline-ready amendment and target a sign date so we can provision for Oct.

Looping in Lauren for billing/co-term handling and Ben for pricing approval.
